narrative: The model estimates a 47% chance that you will fail your final year. Although that is below half, it is still high enough for the school’s system to flag you for remedial courses as a precaution. The strongest reason is that you have said you do not want to continue to higher education; among students who passed, every one wanted higher education. That lack of a longer-term academic goal weighed most heavily toward a failing prediction. Your record of no previous class failures actually worked in your favour, pushing the estimate toward passing. However, your weekly study time of under two hours pushed the other way: most students who passed studied two to five hours a week, while only about one in five studied less than two hours. Your 11 absences, compared with an average of about four among passing students, are also a practical warning sign. To improve, set a clear intention to continue your education, raise study time to at least two to five hours weekly, and reduce absences. Use the family support available to you and ask for help early in subjects where you fall behind.
